Canva AI Video Generator: Create, Download and Check Your Clip

Open Canva AI from the homepage and choose Video clip, then check your account’s access and the selected audio route. After generating, download the clip or open it in the editor. Check the downloaded MP4 below for duration, framing and audio tracks. The current Help page distinguishes eight-second clips with audio from six-second clips without it.

What do you need to do in Canva?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Create a video clip from a prompt

Start at Canva AI on the homepage and select Video clip. Enter an English prompt; optionally attach a reference image. The current Canva Help instructions describe an eight-second route with audio and a six-second route without audio. Check the selected route before expecting sound.

Try a brief with one subject, action and camera movement:

A ceramic mug on a wooden table beside a window.
A slow camera push toward the mug.
Soft morning light; gentle room ambience.
Keep the mug's shape consistent. No text or logos.

This is a prompt to try, not a tested generation result. Put essential action before optional style. Listen to dialogue and effects before keeping a take; describing sound in a prompt does not guarantee the result you want.

Canva saves the result automatically. Use its download icon for the clip, or choose Use Canva Editor to trim it or add text. If generation has not appeared, Canva advises allowing up to two minutes. If it still fails, preserve the error and check usage before submitting another attempt.

Missing, free or a different video feature?

Canva’s feature page lists limited monthly Create a Video Clip access for Pro, Business, Enterprise and Nonprofit users. It does not give a universal monthly count. Read the allowance shown for your account; a free account or plan label alone does not establish access to every generator.

If the clip entry is absent in the video editor, return to Canva AI on the homepage. The current Help page says this entry is not yet available inside video designs in the editor. Magic Media is a separate path; its availability and outputs should not be treated as the same feature.

A talking avatar, an animated photo and a generated scene solve different tasks. Decide whether you need a person reading a script, motion applied to an existing image, or a newly generated shot. Use the product entry for that task instead of buying a plan to solve a missing-button problem.

Download an MP4 and verify the exported clip

In an edited design, select Share → Download → MP4 Video, choose the pages to export, then download. If Canva Free shows an upgrade prompt after you change quality, the download instructions say to keep the default quality and retry. Check paid elements separately.

Play the saved file through to its end. An editor preview, a generated clip and the final multi-page export can have different lengths. Check the downloaded file rather than assuming it retained the original clip’s duration or framing. To combine separate exports, merge the clips into one MP4. To cut the beginning or end after export, trim the MP4 locally. To review a specific moment, extract a PNG frame from the export.

Choose a downloaded video.

The file stays in your browser. The checker reads dimensions, duration and audio track count. It also outlines a centered crop for your chosen canvas. The preview plays the original file. To export a cropped file, use the local video cropper. A yellow border shows the portion a centered fill would keep; objects outside it may be cut off.

Why does my Canva video have no sound?

Play the downloaded MP4 with the player unmuted, then check the file above. MP4 is the export format Canva lists for designs with audio.

  • No audio track. The six-second Canva AI route is silent by design. If you expected sound, reopen the design, check the selected export pages and preview any audio in the timeline. Add an audio track in the editor if needed, export as MP4 and check the new file.
  • One or more audio tracks. A track can be silent. Check the player and device volume first, then compare the same moment in the Canva editor. If the editor is silent too, check the video or audio track’s volume and the track’s position in the timeline.
  • Audio tracks could not be checked. Try a complete MP4 export or inspect the file’s stream information in a desktop video player.

See Canva’s video export and audio track controls. The checker above reads the track list. If it finds one audio track and the clip still seems silent, check the decoded audio signal for that section. Play the clip to verify dialogue, music or effects.

Keep the full frame or fill a vertical canvas

For a 1920 × 1080 landscape clip, filling a 9:16 canvas keeps a central region only 607.5 pixels wide. That is 31.64% of the original frame area. A subject near either edge can disappear even when the exported video has the right dimensions.

Choose between two edits:

  • Keep the whole frame: fit the entire clip inside the canvas and use the surrounding space for a background or captions.
  • Fill the canvas: reposition the crop around the subject and preview the whole shot. Check moving subjects at both ends of the clip.

This checker uses a centered crop, so it cannot predict a manually repositioned or automatically tracked crop. Play the exported file to judge whether the crop still keeps the subject in frame throughout.

Try the checker with a known file

Download an eight-second landscape test clip, then select it above. It is a solid-color video we created locally, not Canva output. Expect 1920 × 1080, eight seconds, and 31.64% frame retention for a portrait canvas, and no audio track.

Download a six-second portrait test clip to check the other case: 1080 × 1920 already fits a 9:16 canvas. The portrait clip also has no audio track.

Compare a test clip with an audible tone and one with a silent audio track. Both report one audio track. Only the first plays an audible tone.

Sources and test scope

Official instructions checked November 24, 2026: Create a video clip, AI video generator access and feature overview, and video download settings. The current Help page’s audio and duration branches are more specific than the marketing page’s eight-second summary.

On November 28 we checked Canva’s export and audio controls documentation. We tested the local checker with synthetic clips with no track, an audible track and a silent track. Those tests cover the file checker. Canva generation, paid accounts and output quality were outside the test. For choosing between services, use the AI video budget comparison.
